source.title: On the geometry of generalization and memorization in deep neural networks
source.authors: Cory Stephenson; Suchismita Padhy; Abhinav Ganesh; Yue Hui; Hanlin Tang; SueYeon Chung

record.file_problem: Full paper text, including supplemental information, is present.
record.tranche_reason: Tests learning and memorization under randomly permuted labels using training/test accuracy, representation geometry, and gradient analysis; it does not reproduce the original studies’ full random-label setup and measures.
record.gate_note: The paper trains on fractions of randomly permuted labels and reports training/test accuracy and other outcomes. Its results on fully permuted labels are not numerically reported in the supplied text; discussion of typical hyperparameters at high permutation fractions is explicitly not shown. Cited results from Zhang et al. (2016) and Arpit et al. (2017) are not this study’s results.
record.test_reason: The study directly measures earlier learning of correct labels and later memorization of corrupted labels, testing V6 with accuracy trajectories and representation analysis. It also reports training fit under partial corruption and a training-hyperparameter qualification relevant to V1.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors conclude that shared class features are learned early, memorization emerges later and mainly in deeper layers, and small early gradient contributions from randomly labeled examples help explain this ordering.
record.recipe_differences: Uses partially permuted labels and analyzes accuracy, manifold geometry, and gradient contributions across layers and epochs. Models were trained with Adam, learning rate 1 × 10−4, batch size 1,024, and no weight decay or other regularization; the authors state these hyperparameters were selected for consistency rather than optimized generalization.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper reports different outcomes by layer and training epoch; high label-permutation fractions may require different training hyperparameters, but those results are not shown.

fits_no_version.finding: Test manifold capacity declines as the corruption fraction increases.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Increasing label corruption reduces linear separability of held-out class representations in the final layer.

fits_no_version.finding: Test accuracy eventually declines during training at fixed 50% label corruption.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Continued training on partially corrupted labels can reduce generalization after its early peak.

record.problems: Most reported accuracy curves are not numerically transcribed in the text. The study focuses on partial label permutation; the authors explicitly say results at high permutation fractions are not shown, and note that typical training hyperparameters may not work well there. The reported V1 test result does not quantify chance-level error.
record.rows_left_out: No rows omitted. Fig. 2 includes accuracy curves across models and datasets, but the supplied text does not give model-specific numerical curve values beyond the qualitative description used in R1–R4. Fig. A.8 shows geometry across permutation fractions; its plotted values are not transcribed, so only the textual summary is recorded in R5.

untested.parts: No explicit zero-error and chance-test-performance result is reported for completely randomized labels. The unchanged-hyperparameter qualification is discussed, but its high-corruption experiments are not shown.
No constant-factor comparison between true-label and fully random-label training times, or convergence-time trend across corruption fractions, is reported.
No shuffled-pixel, independently permuted-pixel, or unstructured Gaussian-noise input experiment is reported. The synthetic spherical-manifold dataset contains class structure.
Perfect training fit throughout the full corruption range and steadily increasing test error toward chance are not established by the supplied accuracy results. Figure A.8 measures geometry instead.
No controlled comparison of weight decay, dropout, or augmentation, or of generalization with and without these regularizers, is reported.
The reported temporal evidence concerns mixed correct and corrupted labels; a matched comparison of entirely correct-label and entirely random-label training trajectories is not established.

missing.what: Explicit incomplete-memorization result for ResNet-18 on Tiny ImageNet after 1,000 epochs. Record this separately from the near-perfect CIFAR-100 training fits.

The authors' reported high-corruption hyperparameter sensitivity: typical settings may train poorly, whereas their reduced learning rate and increased batch size work across corruption fractions at some generalization cost. Outcomes are not numerically shown.

Direct temporal representation evidence: permuted manifolds remain near their capacity lower bound at peak generalization, then become separable in later layers at the final epoch, while restored-label structure deteriorates there.

record.verdict_notes: Partial label corruption is the experimental manipulation being tested, so it does not disqualify these memorization experiments. Missing numerical timing or chance-level accuracy is untested coverage, not evidence against the claims. The statement that no regularization was used conflicts with dropout entries in the VGG-16 architecture table; neither establishes a controlled V5 test.

versions.untested_parts: The text does not report a numerical result for the 100% permutation condition or state that test error is at chance in that condition; it focuses on partially permuted labels for reported results.

The text says more epochs are required and permuted examples quickly converge once they begin, but does not quantify a constant-factor training-time comparison or report convergence time across corruption fractions.
Shuffled pixels, independently permuted pixels, and Gaussian-noise inputs are not tested.

The paper discusses a range of permutation fractions and reports test-manifold capacity trends, but the accuracy curves across fractions are figure-only and do not provide extractable numerical results in the supplied text.
The study says it does not use weight decay or other regularization, but does not compare regularization methods or test generalization after removing them.

The study tests partially permuted labels and reports early learning of shared features, but does not compare a fully random-label dataset against an otherwise identical real-label-only training condition.

rows.subject: VGG-16
rows.operation_detail: Trained on CIFAR-100 with 50% of labels randomly permuted; accuracy tracked over training.
rows.note: The paper describes the plotted training accuracy as near 100%; the sentence refers to the tested networks, while the text presents VGG-16 in detail.
rows.check: Near-perfect training accuracy at 50% corruption measures V4's training-fit component. It does not establish V1's completely random labeling condition or V6's temporal ordering. Retain the VGG-16 attribution; the general statement about tested networks has an explicit Tiny ImageNet exception in Section 3.1.

rows.note: Text describes a decrease, but gives no test accuracy value or chance-level comparison.

rows.subject: VGG-16
rows.operation_detail: Tracked accuracy on permuted examples during training on CIFAR-100.
rows.measure: Accuracy on permuted examples over training
rows.value: More epochs are required to fit the permuted examples; these examples quickly converge once they begin.
rows.note: The authors report the qualitative timing pattern without epoch counts or a constant-factor comparison.
rows.check: Delayed learning of permuted examples supports V6. Comparing subsets within one mixed-label training run does not measure V2's training-time ratio between true-label and random-label runs or convergence time across corruption fractions.

rows.subject: VGG-16
rows.operation_detail: Tracked accuracy on restored examples, which use the correct labels for examples trained with permuted labels.
rows.measure: Accuracy on restored examples over training
rows.value: Before the permuted examples are learned, many are actually classified as their correct label.
rows.note: The authors interpret this as evidence that the network has learned features that generalize beyond correctly labeled training examples.
rows.check: The restored-label accuracy increase before random-label learning directly supports earlier acquisition of shared class features.

rows.subject: VGG-16

rows.value: decreases significantly with increasing permutation fraction
rows.note: This is a representation-geometry measure, not test error; the accuracy-versus-fraction results are shown in a figure without extractable values in the supplied text.
rows.check: Test manifold capacity measures representation separability, not training error or test error. Figure A.8 contains manifold-capacity curves across corruption fractions, not accuracy curves.
